$description: WCAG contrast gate for the token generator. Every rule is checked for every theme; themes whose role is highContrast are held to at least `highContrastMin`. Failures fail the build.

rules.note: body text on the panel ground
landing screen text on the darker end of its ground
landing screen captions on the darker end of its ground
the brand mark's S and the wordmark's "Studio" — 3.0 is the WCAG threshold for a graphic that carries meaning, not the 4.5 used for text
type on the chrome bar and on Light's landing card
the brand mark's S where it sits on the chrome bar; the E uses chromeInk there, which every theme already gates
the label of an affirmative AppButton
an affirmative AppButton against the dialog ground it sits on
the active workspace tab's label on the chrome bar

baselineNote: Known failures recorded when each theme was introduced, so the gate could be switched on without changing a colour. Each is a WCAG failure that has not been fixed. The gate still fails if one regresses below its recorded value, and this list must only shrink. Dark has the one entry, accentFg/purple at 2.88, the lowest ratio the set has had: the theme never puts text on an accent fill, so accentFg stays inherited white while purple is the lighter #AA83F6. Light's entry, white on #9B6DFF at 3.49, went when the theme became Light (ES-751) and took a deepened blue accent, 5.64 under white; its textMuted/bgBase entry went earlier, when the body tokens became the light palette. Classic and High Contrast had entries until the 2026-09 remake moved Classic's purple to #7C4DFF (4.81 under white) and its textMuted to #6B7A99 (4.27 on bgBase), and High Contrast's textMuted to #A6A6A6 (8.63 on black).
